biography.ja: ドイツ・ケルンに生まれ、パリに渡ってアレヴィらに師事した後、チェロ奏者として活動しつつ自ら小劇場を興し、風刺の効いた軽妙なオペレッタで一世を風靡した。晩年は唯一の本格的なオペラに取り組んだが、完成を見ないまま世を去った。
biography.en: Born in Cologne, Germany, he moved to Paris and studied under Halévy among others. While working as a cellist he founded his own small theater and became the toast of the city with witty, satirical operettas. In his final years he undertook his one full-scale serious opera but died before completing it.

style.ja: 軽快でリズミカルな旋律と、社会風刺を織り込んだ機知に富んだ台本を組み合わせ、「オペレッタ」というジャンルをほぼ一人で確立した。代表作の一つは、グルックが確立した神話劇の格式を意図的にパロディ化した内容で、当時の観客に衝撃と笑いを同時にもたらした。
style.en: He combined light, rhythmic melody with witty librettos laced with social satire, single-handedly establishing the genre of operetta almost on his own. One of his best-known works deliberately parodies the solemn mythological grandeur that Gluck had established, delivering both shock and laughter to audiences of the day.

impact.ja: 「オペレッタの父」として、後のウィーンのオペレッタ様式や、さらにミュージカルというジャンルの成立にまで連なる系譜の源流となった。唯一の本格的なオペラは未完のまま遺されたが、他者の補筆によって上演され続けており、風刺喜劇と真摯な悲劇の両方に才能を示した作曲家として記憶されている。
impact.en: As the "father of operetta" he became the wellspring for a lineage running through the later Viennese operetta tradition and eventually into the musical as a genre. His one full-scale serious opera was left unfinished at his death but continues to be staged in completions by others, and he is remembered as a composer who showed talent in both satirical comedy and earnest tragedy.
